subject: Nebula Biotech — unit pricing follow-up & host comparisons
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nebula Biotech discovery recap — pricing bands and quick benchmark

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick written recap and the numbers you asked for so we have a single source-of-truth. I attached the usage sample you sent and a short benchmark PDF comparing per-1M token economics across common hosts.

Key notes from the call:
- Current weekly/aggregate: ~50M tokens/month expected initially, with spikes up to ~120M in peak weeks tied to model evaluation runs.
- Traffic profile: bursty (hour-level spikes), some nightly batch jobs, and low-latency inference for production endpoints (~120ms p95 target).
- Primary constraint: predictability of unit cost and avoidance of token tax during spikes.
- Security/compliance: you need SOC2 evidence — we covered private deployment options but initial pilot will be hosted.

Benchmark (rough, per-1M tokens; normalized to comparable chat-style workload):
- Redwood (open-model optimized / quantized Llama-family): $6.00 / 1M tokens (standard serving profile)
- Redwood — with premium SLA / reserved capacity: $4.50 / 1M (committed, 12-month)
- OpenAI (current equivalent conversational model offering): $14.00 / 1M
- Anthropic (conversational family): $13.50 / 1M
- Other open-model hosts (varies by quantization & batching): $5.00–$10.00 / 1M

Notes on the numbers above:
- Redwood listed prices reflect typical serving configuration (fp16/quantized) and default batching — actual unit cost can fall with prefix/KV caching and smart batching for repeated calls.
- OpenAI/Anthropic numbers reflect hosted managed models with their platform overhead — higher baseline for fully managed opaque endpoints.
- The premium SLA/reserved capacity price is intended for committed volumes (we model at 50M+ tokens/mo).

Suggested next steps:
1) Pilot: 1–2M tokens at $9 / 1M for the pilot period (1 month) — this covers burst handling, baseline tuning, and integration checks.
2) Commitment pricing: if you commit to ~50M tokens/mo for a 6–12 month term, we can target $6 / 1M (with options to go to $4.50 / 1M for annual reserved pools).
3) Provide the sample usage CSV you shared and we will run a 72-hour simulation to validate unit-cost sensitivity and expected p95 latency.

Attachments: nebula-usage-sample.csv, redwood-benchmark-1M-comparison.pdf

If this looks right, I’ll put together a short pilot SOW and a HubSpot quote link.

Thanks — Sergio

FYI — Nebula is interested and has a budget sensitivity that maps to a target blended $/1M of roughly $5–$9 depending on commitments. They asked for: pilot at $9/1M (agreed verbally), 72-hour simulation, and a HubSpot quote for procurement.

Request: can we approve the following for the initial commercial outreach?
- Pilot: 2M tokens @ $9 / 1M (1 month). No discount required — this covers runtime validation.
- Pilot -> Commitment glide path: if they commit to >=50M tokens/mo for 6 months, transition price to $6 / 1M. For annual reserved capacity 12mo, target $4.50 / 1M.
- Approval band: I’m asking for clearance to offer up to 20% off the $6 / 1M committed price through promotional credit if necessary.

Why this structure?
- Protects unit economics during the pilot (pilot higher price) while giving a clear path to competitive committed pricing — we win bench vs OpenAI/Anthropic at the $6 / 1M level and beat other hosts in many configs.
- Leaves room to use credits instead of permanent list-price discounts for early-stage accounts.

Attachments: feeder (the CSV Alex sent) and benchmark PDF for reference. Links to HubSpot deal included below.

Can finance sign off on the 20% promotional credit option? Marissa — can you prep a one-page SOW (pilot + acceptance criteria) and a draft HubSpot quote? Ben — any concerns on SLA or escalation if they exceed peak capacity during the experiment window?

Thanks — Sergio
